question: Does an exact fixed R8 neurosecretory/antigen RNA panel show a useful fusion-partner-associated native EMC phenotype beyond established partner/high-grade associations? Independent source/prior-art/value review only, pending exact owner proposal.
prospective_limit: Previous panel values are known. No claim of blinding or pristine preregistration. Selection remains exploratory, and original full panel family plus prior tested contrasts must be disclosed. No matrix or new gene values inspected in this review.
approach: Reuse R1–R9 source gates, original R8 panel specification and native labels. Inspect primary eligibility/library methods and published prior-art scope, not result cells. No new source retrieval before distinct ownership/source coordination.
validity_requirements: Actual specimen-to-partner molecular labels with complete native donor/condition map, no inferred label from morphology, accession adjacency or source marker expression.
All eligible public native EMC conditions and all fixed panel family retained; paired handling and technical replicate sensitivity, overlap accounted.
Evaluate grade/morphology, sex, age/site, preservation/capture/batch, stromal purity and partner-growth association as alternatives.
RNA empirical association is allowed; protein accessibility, secretion, target dependency or fusion-forming mechanism are outside inference.
useful_consequence: A specific testable disease association may change the next orthogonal marker/compartment measurement even without therapy inference. General TAF15 high-grade phenotype or a selected favorable marker does not suffice.
defeat: Published exact contrast, invalid/unresolvable partner labels, confounded/unreplicated association, or outcome-selected partial panel with no honest family correction stops proposed numerical stage.
restrictions: Original freezes immutable; only owned output; denied FAP/glycan/HLA/structural mechanism content closed; quiet source/file work, no private/login/bypass/spend/outreach/publication/PR/shared writes/push.
